_initial_state_note: Replaces the old num_incumbent_cohorts warm start (simulated cohorts admitted at negative terms). The university starts NOT empty: 'occupancy' is how many seats in each course are already taken by the existing student body the first simulated cohort competes against -- a steady-state background load subtracted from that course's free seats on every mandatory term (see src/simulator.py::_effective_capacity and CLAUDE.md's Initial-State Model). 'standing' is a rough head-count of existing students at each year-standing, added as a constant to the aggregate stage-flow chart so it starts non-empty. Edit these in Settings or the Scenario Builder. num_incumbent_cohorts still works as an engine knob (defaults to 0 / no incumbents) but is no longer part of the default plan.
_optional_terms_note: Fall and Spring are mandatory (the only seasons that advance a student's personal_semester clock / max_terms budget; see CLAUDE.md's Term/Season Model). Winter and Summer are optional intersessions: courses must explicitly list 'Winter'/'Summer' in their own offering array to run then, and get a smaller capacity than their mandatory-term seats -- optional_term_capacity_scale x course.capacity (see CLAUDE.md's Term/Season Model). admit_interval_terms was raised from 2 to 4 to keep yearly, Fall-only admissions now that the cycle is 4 terms long instead of 2. Only cs_core courses are offered optionally -- math/english/gen_ed courses are deliberately excluded: they're tier-2 (lowest) enrollment priority, so cs_core crowds them out of every regular term's load cap, building a multi-year backlog that would swamp a scaled-down bonus offering (observed: ~1000+ capacity blocks on a single gen-ed course vs ~250 on the CS gateway) -- a real, if disproportionate, finding worth knowing about even though it's out of scope for this illustrative default. optional_terms_enabled defaults to FALSE: Winter/Summer are off (legacy 2-season Fall/Spring cycle) until an admin switches them on in Settings -> PUT /config. All the data above (terms_per_year, mandatory_terms, optional_term_capacity_scale, and the admit_interval_terms=4 yearly cadence) stays in this file inert the whole time; flipping the flag on re-activates it with no re-entry needed. admit_interval_terms auto-rescales to 2 while the flag is off, so Fall-only yearly admission is preserved either way -- see src/models/semester.py::effective_admit_interval_terms.
_registration_tier_note: Seat-priority bands by completed_ch, checked in descending order (registration_tier 0 = registers first). QU's real priority-registration policy; a different institution redefines its own bands here, not in student.py::registration_tier.
_year_standing_note: Ascending completed-CH cutoffs for the flow chart's Year1->Year2->Year3->Year4 stage nodes. QU's actual 4-year/120-CH bands (30 CH/year); a program with a different total credit-hour count sets its own bands here, not in student.py::curriculum_stage.
_on_time_note: Semesters-to-graduate cutoff for the on_time_rate metric (finished at/under this counts as 'on time'). QU's standard 4-year/8-semester schedule; a program with a different standard length sets its own value here, not in analytics.py.
_enrollment_priority_note: Phase-1 desired-enrollment order, tried after retakes (which always come first and are not part of this list). Each tier is {categories: [...], min_ch?: N}; a student's eligible courses are bucketed into the first tier whose categories contains the course's category AND whose min_ch (default 0) the student's completed_ch already meets, then tiers are filled in order up to the load cap. A category absent from every tier, or gated by an unmet min_ch, is simply not enrolled that term. This is QU CS's policy (required courses, then cs_electives once junior-standing CH is reached, then service/gen-ed courses) expressed as data; a different program redefines its own tiers/categories here, not in student.py.
_dropout_note: Dropout has three causes. PRIMARY (GPA): each term a student with completed_ch >= probation_min_ch and gpa < dropout_gpa_floor leaves with probability base_hazard*(1+(floor-gpa)), doubled (early_multiplier) in their first dropout_early_sem_cutoff semesters. SECONDARY (gateway): failing one course dropout_fails_threshold times drops them with prob dropout_prob_on_repeated_fail. TERTIARY (cumulative delay, opt-in via dropout_delay_hazard_scale, default 0.0 = off): independent of GPA, a student whose completed_ch has fallen behind the pace implied by on_time_terms faces a per-term hazard of dropout_delay_hazard_scale * (credit-hour deficit / total program CH) -- models real students who withdraw once they've fallen far enough behind, rather than passively riding it out to CENSORED at the horizon. Left at 0.0 for the calibrated QU baseline (untested against real QU data, unlike the two hazards above); an admin can opt in per plan. CALIBRATION SCOPE: the only QU anchor (scripts/analyze_qu_data.py) is the AGGREGATE 72.3% 12-semester graduation rate — the open data is semester-level counts, not student-level histories, so dropout TIMING cannot be validated. The early_multiplier front-loading is a face-validity assumption, not a data fit. UPDATE (post optional-term model): a 30-seed sweep of base_hazard over 0.15-0.21 now moves graduation by 0.78pp (0.7382 -> 0.7304) with dropout/censored moving in opposite directions -- a real, monotone relationship, not the flat dropped<->censored trade found before optional terms existed. This swing is now LARGER than the gateway-capacity sweep's ~0.1pp (see _sections_note) -- the reverse of the original ranking. See docs/project_overview.md for how dropout/GPA mechanics work.
